sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Understand Anything is a Claude Code plugin that turns a codebase, knowledge base or docs into an interactive knowledge graph. You can explore it in a dashboard, search it, take guided tours and ask questions about how things fit together.
sixtySeconds.problem: Joining a large codebase is overwhelming. This plugin scans every file, function, class and dependency with a multi-agent pipeline and gives you plain-English summaries, architecture layers and tours in the right order.
whoFor: Developers onboarding to a new codebase
Product managers who want to see business flows in code
Anyone with a large docs or wiki collection
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want an explorable map with summaries and guided tours inside your agent. The first analysis can use a lot of tokens on big projects, so a subscription or local model is recommended.
requirements: Claude Code (also works with Devin, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and more)
A token plan, subscription or local model for large projects

overview: Running /understand starts a multi-agent pipeline that extracts files, functions, classes and dependencies and saves a knowledge graph to .ua/knowledge-graph.json. /understand-dashboard opens an interactive web view, colour-coded by architectural layer, where each node shows its code, relationships and an explanation.

A domain view maps code to business processes. Other commands answer questions about the codebase, analyse the impact of your current changes, explain a specific file, and generate an onboarding guide. /understand-knowledge builds a graph from an LLM-style wiki.

The dashboard adapts its detail for junior developers, PMs or power users, and explains 12 programming concepts in context. Output can be generated in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian or Vietnamese.
